children: The September CPI inflation print is creating a significant dilemma for Federal Reserve policy just weeks before the October meeting, according to Craig Shapiro, senior macro strategist at NinjaTrader Live.
hotter than expected, rising 0.6% on the month and 3.7% year-over-year, with core CPI advancing 0.3% month-over-month.
The data contradicted recent guidance from Fed officials who had talked down the odds of an October rate hike from roughly 68% to below 20% over the past two weeks.
Core inflation breadth widened significantly in September, worsening on what Fed Governor Warsh has identified as a key metric.
Fifty-nine of 113 core items ran at a 3%+ annualized pace, up from 49, and services is where inflation is spreading, Shapiro said, with 31 items now above 3% year-over-year, up from 27.
Service sector prices increased 0.4% on the month and are up 3.1% from one year ago.
The CPI diffusion indexes showed over 60% of weighted components advancing above 3%, observed Joseph Brusuelas, RSM principal and chief economist. This undermines expectations for cooling inflation.

"All of those making the case that inflation would cool or see mild disinflation—it is not in the data," he said, warning that "we could easily get a December holiday gift of a 50 bps hike" if underlying inflation pressures do not abate.
In addition, real average hourly earnings declined 0.7% from one year ago, marking the sixth consecutive monthly decline and intensifying the cost-of-living crisis for American households.
Market uncertainty remains elevated heading into Fed Governor Warsh's scheduled speech Thursday night, the last word before the pre-meeting blackout period begins.
"The problem for risk assets isn't a hike. It's that nobody knows what the Fed will do," Shapiro said, noting that the bond market responded with a front-end-led bear flattener, with two-year yields
near 5.67% and bond futures turning negatively convex for the first time since 2007, he cautioned traders to "respect size, especially Thursday night when Warsh hits thin Globex liquidity."

title: September CPI data creates dilemma for Warsh weeks before October decision
